note: Curated coding problem bank for CareerLift AI Phase 2 (Secure Coding Arena). Each problem is SERVER-owned. Hidden test cases are NEVER exposed to the client. concept_ids map into agent/data/concepts.json so a correct solution feeds the shared Phase 0 mastery model. I/O is line-based over stdin/stdout so a single solution shape works across Java, Python and C++.
io_convention: Programs read from standard input and write to standard output. Each test case's `stdin` is fed verbatim; the program's stdout is compared to `stdout` after trailing-whitespace normalisation per line.

problems.title: Sum of Two Numbers
problems.description: Read two integers and print their sum. This warm-up checks that you can read input, compute a result, and print it in the required format.
problems.input_format: A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.
problems.output_format: A single line containing the integer a + b.

problems.title: Maximum in a List
problems.description: Given n integers, print the largest one. A single linear pass is enough — this is an O(n) scan.
problems.input_format: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
problems.output_format: A single line with the maximum of the n integers.

examples.explanation: 9 is the largest of the five values.

problems.title: Factorial (Recursion)
problems.description: Compute n! = 1 x 2 x ... x n. A natural recursive solution needs a correct base case (0! = 1). The answer fits in a 64-bit signed integer for the given range.
problems.input_format: A single line containing an integer n.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description: Given a SORTED array of n distinct integers and a target, print the 0-based index of the target, or -1 if it is not present. An O(log n) binary search is expected; the array is already sorted in non-decreasing order.
problems.input_format: Line 1: integers n and target. Line 2: n space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.
problems.output_format: The 0-based index of target, or -1 if absent.

problems.title: Count Pairs With Given Sum
problems.description: Given n integers and a target k, count the number of unordered index pairs (i, j), i < j, whose values sum to k. A hash map gives an average O(n) solution; a naive O(n^2) double loop may exceed the time limit on the largest hidden cases.
problems.input_format: Line 1: integers n and k. Line 2: n space-separated integers.
problems.output_format: A single line with the number of valid pairs.

problems.title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
problems.description: Given n closed intervals, merge all overlapping (or touching) intervals and print the result sorted by start. The expected approach sorts by start (O(n log n)) then sweeps once; its worst case is dominated by the sort, not the sweep.
problems.input_format: Line 1: integer n. Each of the next n lines: two integers l r (l <= r).
problems.output_format: The merged intervals, one per line as `l r`, sorted by start.
constraints: intervals that merely touch (e.g. [1 2] and [2 3]) are merged
